title: ⭐ Practice: what you like, and how you say it

questions.prompt: Sonia answers: "The lyrics, mostly. I always listen to the words before anything else." Which question was she asked?

options.text: What do you like in a hit?
What type of hits do you like?

questions.explanation: "What do you like in a hit?" asks which part of a song you enjoy, and the lesson gives four possible answers to it: the singer, the music, the melody and the lyrics. Sonia hands back one of the four. A question about the type of hits would be answered by a kind of music — rap, rock, jazz; a question about her favourite song calls for a title; and a question about her favourite singer calls for a name. Read an answer closely and it gives you back its own question.

questions.prompt: At the security check, the officer tells Tina: "You mustn't take that bottle through." What does Tina have to do?

options.text: Take it through, but keep it closed.
Ask a second officer for permission.
Nothing: she may keep it if she wants to.

questions.explanation: "Mustn't" forbids. The officer is not giving advice and is not saying that the bottle is unnecessary, so the bottle stays behind. Reading mustn't as "you don't have to" is the classic mistake of this lesson: that meaning belongs to don't have to, as in "You don't have to run, we have twenty minutes." A ban is not a matter of opinion either, so asking somebody else will not lift it, and carrying the bottle through with the cap screwed on breaks it just the same.

questions.prompt: Complete: "Nothing could shake her ___ in her own voice: she went on singing when everyone around her had given up."
questions.explanation: Faith is what you believe in and the trust you put in it, so faith in her own voice is exactly what keeps her singing when nobody else believes. Fate is almost the opposite idea — what is meant to happen to you whatever you do — and nobody can shake it. Sorrow is deep sadness and memory is what you keep of what is gone; neither can stand in front of "in her own voice". One single sound separates faith from fate, and everything else separates them too.

questions.prompt: Two words make a minimal pair when ONE single sound separates them and the rest is identical. Which of these is a minimal pair?
questions.explanation: Song and sung are identical except for their vowel, and that one vowel carries the whole difference — a textbook minimal pair, like them and then or love and luck. The three others merely sound close. Melody and memory share their rhythm and their ending but differ in two places inside the word; singer and single part company after "sing-"; and eternity and eternal are two forms of one family, with a different number of syllables and a different ending. Count the differences before you use the term.

questions.prompt: You are at the check-in desk and you would like to keep a small bag with you in the cabin. Which sentence asks the clerk for permission?

options.text: Must I take this bag with me on the plane?
Can I take this bag with me on the plane?
Can you take this bag with me on the plane?
I can take this bag with me on the plane.

questions.explanation: English asks for permission with "Can I…?", and the subject has to be the person who wants to act — you. "Must I…?" would ask whether you are obliged to carry the bag, which is not what you want to know; putting "you" in the question sends the clerk on board with your luggage; and the last sentence states a permission instead of asking for one, which is precisely what you cannot do at a desk where somebody else decides.

questions.prompt: A magazine writes about "her sudden fame". Tick every word that could replace "fame" here.
questions.explanation: Renown is fame itself — the lesson puts celebrity, fame and renown together as one idea — and stardom names the state of being famous as a performer, so "her sudden stardom" says what "her sudden fame" says. The other three name other things entirely: prowess is great skill, and a singer can have it for years without anybody knowing her name; sorrow is deep sadness; and fate is what is meant to happen to you whatever you do. Being good, being sad and being destined are three different things from being known.
